name: Acute Infantile Liver Failure-Multisystemic Involvement Syndrome
aliases: Infantile Acute Liver Failure with Multisystemic Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Acute Infantile Liver Failure Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Rapid onset of liver failure with coagulopathy and jaundice in infancy
Evidence of involvement of at least two other organ systems (e.g., renal, neurological, hematological)
Exclusion of infectious, metabolic, and toxic causes of liver failure
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes if available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of acute liver failure with coagulopathy and jaundice plus multisystemic involvement, after exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not mandatory

searchTerms: sudden brain dysfunction from liver failure
acute brain swelling due to liver problems
confusion and brain symptoms from liver failure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe coagulopathy unresponsive to vitamin K
searchTerms: severe bleeding disorder not helped by vitamin K
blood clotting failure resistant to vitamin K
uncontrolled bleeding despite vitamin K treatment

pathognomonic.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera
searchTerms: yellow skin and eyes with very high bilirubin
marked jaundice with elevated bilirubin levels

common.notes: Elevated creatinine and decreased urine output
Low blood glucose due to impaired gluconeogenesis
Low platelet count contributing to bleeding risk

occasional.notes: Secondary to metabolic disturbances or encephalopathy
Fluid accumulation in lungs due to multisystem failure
Low blood pressure from systemic involvement
Small red or purple spots due to bleeding

rare.notes: Paralysis or weakness of eye muscles
Irregular heart rhythms secondary to metabolic imbalance
Hearing impairment due to nerve involvement

laboratory: Marked elevation of serum transaminases (AST, ALT)
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly with heterogeneous echotexture
Brain MRI may show cerebral edema in encephalopathy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with mitochondrial or metabolic liver diseases (if identified)
other: Liver biopsy showing massive hepatic necrosis (if performed)
Exclusion of infectious and metabolic etiologies

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive liver failure with mitochondrial DNA mutations
May have different multisystemic involvement pattern

redFlags: Rapid progression to hepatic encephalopathy within days
Uncorrectable coagulopathy despite vitamin K administration
Multisystem organ failure in an infant
